Wonderfully preserved piece of history
Aug 2019
Part of the Continental Hotel, the oldest (I think) hotel in Saigon, with a history to match, including Malraux and Greene, continuing through the Vietnam war (or the American war as the Vietnamese refer to it, this restaurant is beautifully preserved, from the ceiling plaster work to the columns.

It is situated opposite the equally beautiful Opera House, and the Caravelle Hotel.

The food is good but not exceptional, but still very good value for money: it is the ambience of the place itself which makes this a top experience.

Sad
Jan 2019 • Friends
Yes, we came here like many other people to see the ghost of Graham Greene. But he has definitely checked out of the hotel. The restaurant, which I had also picked as we were having lunch with a senior government official and I wanted it to be a little impressive, was empty, sad, down-in-the-heels, and worst of all, felt inauthentic. The remaining pillars seemed fake, the gold capitals on the pillars were plastic, the service was poor to non-existant, the whole place was shabby and not in a historic way. The room is characterless and everyone (except us) seemed to know that because we were the only people in the restaurant. Nevertheless service was slow. All of us had soup and salad, and I have to say the food was not too bad. I had a shrimp cesar salad that was pretty good. The lobster bisque was just OK. It's hard to recommend this restaurant as having even a glimmer of old world charm.
